title: The Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS) dataset
description: The Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS) dataset comprises 128 nights of simultaneous polysomnography (PSG) and wearable EEG headband recordings from 108 unique participants, designed to validate wearable EEG technology against clinical PSG for sleep monitoring. The dataset includes human-consensus sleep stage labels derived from expert scoring of PSG recordings, as well as AI-generated sleep stage labels for both PSG and wearable EEG data using a deep learning model. Additional demographic metadata (age, sex, BMI) are provided for each participant, offering a comprehensive resource for sleep staging research and wearable EEG validation.
methods_description: PSG recordings were obtained using a Brain Quick Plus Evolution system by Micromed, capturing EEG, EOG, EMG, respiratory, and PPG signals, while simultaneous wearable EEG recordings were collected using a Bitbrain forehead headband with EEG, IMU, and PPG sensors. Sleep stages were manually scored by three independent expert scorers following AASM criteria, with consensus labels derived from majority agreement (a fourth scorer resolved ties). A deep learning model was trained on the human-consensus labels to generate automatic sleep stage predictions for both PSG and wearable EEG data.
